title: What to expect from a removals company
summary: What a professional firm handles, what they will ask before quoting, and how to compare the responses you receive.
imageAlt: A removals crew carrying wrapped furniture from a house to a Luton van

sections.heading: Start with the whole move, not a single load
paragraphs: A removals company plans the day around the property, not around one vehicle. Give them the collection and destination addresses, the size of each property, your preferred date and whether the two ends are on the same day or split across a move-out and move-in.

Say early if anything falls outside a standard household load: a piano, garden machinery, a workshop, large mirrors or artwork, a loft or garage that has not been cleared, or items going into storage rather than to the new address.
checklist: Both full addresses, not just postcodes
Property size at each end, and the floor you are on
Preferred date, and whether it is fixed to a completion
Rooms, lofts, garages and outbuildings in scope
Anything going to storage instead of the new address

sections.heading: Expect a survey before a firm price
paragraphs: Most established firms will want to see the property before committing to a price, either in person or over a video call. A survey lets them size the crew and the vehicles, spot access problems and quote for packing materials accurately. It is the main reason a removals quote is more reliable than an online estimate.
Treat a firm price given without any survey with some caution on a larger move. It is usually either a provisional figure that can change on the day, or it is carrying a margin to cover the unknown.

sections.heading: Compare what is included, not just the total
paragraphs: Two quotes for the same move can differ because one includes full packing and the other does not. Check what each covers: packing and materials, dismantling and reassembly, appliance disconnection, floor and door protection, storage, and the number of crew and vehicles.

Ask what liability cover is included as standard and what it actually pays out on. Ask whether the price is fixed or hourly, what happens if completion is delayed, and whether waiting time is chargeable. On a chain move, a delayed key release is common enough that it is worth settling in advance.
checklist: Packing, materials and unpacking
Dismantling and reassembly of furniture
Number of crew and vehicles
Liability cover and its limits
Fixed or hourly, and the delay policy

sections.heading: Check the company, not only the quote
paragraphs: Public profiles may show verification and published customer reviews where that information is available. Use them alongside the quote rather than in place of it. A written quote, a named contact and a clear cancellation policy are reasonable to expect from any firm you are seriously considering.
A quote is not a confirmed booking by itself. Agree the final scope, the date, the arrival window, the payment terms and the contact details directly with the company before the move.

title: How to prepare for moving day
summary: A room-by-room plan for the weeks before, the access and parking detail crews need, and the final hour before the vans arrive.
imageAlt: Labelled packing boxes stacked in a hallway before a house move

sections.heading: Confirm the inventory well before the day
paragraphs: Walk every room, plus the loft, garage, shed and anything stored outside, and agree with the company what is in scope. If the load has changed materially since the survey — a sofa sold, a wardrobe added, a garage that turned out to be full — tell them before the day so the crew size and vehicle plan can be corrected.
Decide what is not moving. Items being sold, given away or disposed of should leave before the crew arrives, not be sorted on the doorstep while a van waits.
checklist: Loft, garage, shed and outbuildings cleared or confirmed
Items being sold or disposed of removed beforehand
Anything going to storage separated and labelled
Changes since the survey reported to the company

sections.heading: Pack by room and label for the destination
paragraphs: If you are packing yourself, label every box with the room it is going to at the new address, not the room it came from. That single change removes most of the repeated lifting at the other end. Keep boxes to a weight one person can carry, fill voids so contents cannot shift, and mark fragile boxes on the sides as well as the top.

Keep fixings from dismantled furniture in a labelled bag taped to the item. Pack a first-night box — kettle, bedding, chargers, toiletries, tools, medication — and keep it with you rather than in the van.

sections.heading: Sort access and parking at both ends
paragraphs: Access decides how long a move takes as much as volume does. Check parking restrictions, permits and loading bays at both addresses, and arrange a suspension with the council if a large vehicle cannot get close. In a flat or an office, confirm lift dimensions, booking requirements and any permitted hours for the goods lift.

Tell the company about long carries, narrow stairs, low arches and unadopted or single-track roads. A crew that arrives expecting a driveway and finds a two-hundred-metre carry will lose hours that were not in the quote.
checklist: Parking permits or bay suspensions arranged
Lift booked, with dimensions and permitted hours
Long carries, stairs and access limits reported
Building management notified where required

sections.heading: Plan around the chain, not the clock
paragraphs: On a completion-day move, keys rarely release exactly when expected. Agree with the company what happens if the destination is not available by a certain time, whether the load can stay on the vehicle overnight and what that costs. Keep the estate agent's and solicitor's numbers to hand along with the crew's.
Utilities, the meter readings and the post redirection are yours, not the removals company's. Do them in the days before rather than on the morning itself.

sections.heading: Do a final walkthrough before the vans leave
paragraphs: Check every room, cupboard and the loft hatch against your inventory before the last vehicle leaves. Take meter readings, photograph the empty rooms, and keep documents, valuables, keys and personal items with you rather than in the load.

At the destination, tell the crew where the larger items go before unloading starts. Once the vans are empty, walk them through with the crew leader, compare against the inventory and report any damage promptly and in writing while the detail is fresh.

title: How removals quotes are priced
summary: What actually drives a removals price — volume, access, crew and distance — and how to describe your move so the quotes you get are comparable.
imageAlt: A removals surveyor assessing furniture and measuring a room

sections.heading: Volume is the starting point, not the whole price
paragraphs: Removals firms estimate volume in cubic feet or cubic metres, and that figure sets the vehicle plan. But two three-bedroom houses can differ by a third in volume, which is why bedroom count alone produces unreliable quotes. A survey exists to replace the guess with a measurement.
The rest of the price comes from labour hours, distance and materials. A compact load up four flights of stairs can cost more than a larger load into a bungalow with a driveway.
checklist: Property size and number of rooms in scope
Large or awkward items listed individually
Access at both ends: stairs, lifts, carry distance
Distance between the two addresses

sections.heading: Packing is the biggest optional line
paragraphs: Full packing — where the crew boxes everything, including kitchens and wardrobes — is typically the largest choice you make after volume. Part packing, where the company handles only fragile items, china and artwork, sits in between. Materials are usually charged separately from the labour.
If you are comparing quotes, make sure they assume the same packing arrangement. This is the most common reason two prices for one move look nothing alike.

sections.heading: Ask how the price behaves if the day changes
paragraphs: Find out whether the quote is fixed or an hourly rate with an estimate attached, and what triggers a change. Waiting time on a delayed completion, an extra vehicle, an overnight hold of the load, or a second trip because the inventory grew are the usual variables.
Also confirm the cancellation and postponement terms. On a chain move the date can slip through no fault of yours, and firms differ considerably in how they treat that.
checklist: Fixed price or hourly with an estimate
Waiting-time and delayed-completion charges
Overnight storage of a loaded vehicle
Cancellation and date-change terms

sections.heading: Give every company the same brief
paragraphs: Comparable quotes need a comparable description. Send the same inventory, the same access notes and the same date to each firm, and tell each one whether you want packing quoted. If one company surveys the property and another does not, the two figures are not measuring the same thing.

Update everyone if something changes materially. A late addition of a garage full of tools or the discovery that the new property has no vehicle access will change the plan, and it is cheaper to know two weeks out than on the morning.
